That path binds the issue by repository ID and issue index, then checks repository permission to write issues or pull requests before resolving assignees or invoking the mutation service. The supplied premise makes that permission false, so the handler returns forbidden at the authorization control and does not reach assignee resolution or mutation. The issue-write token scope is distinct from repository issue-write permission and does not satisfy this control. The requested existing issue and assignee, and the authenticated caller, are accepted task premises at the declared boundary rather than independently inferred deployment facts. The source-visible decision is therefore deny. The permission-granted/existing-assignee counterfactual reaches resolution and mutation; the permission-granted/missing-assignee counterfactual reaches resolution but stops on the missing-assignee error before mutation. Source discovery is not-tested, so this result makes no repository-wide or deployment claim.

The strongest visible authorization control requires repository permission to write issues or pull requests and returns forbidden before later processing when absent.
Only after the repository permission check does the path resolve requested assignee names to user IDs.
A nonexistent requested assignee takes an error-return path before the mutation call.
When add mode is active and assignee resolution succeeds, the path invokes the service that adds assignees to the issue.
